jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Burundi's main recorded AI-relevant instrument is Law No. 1/03 of 10 March 2026 on the protection of personal data, which is in force and sets rules on decisions based on automated processing, including an individual explanation and the right to a new decision taken by a human. The Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy leads digital policy and reports holding a workshop in November 2025 to assess the national AI landscape. A national AI strategy for 2025-2030 is reported as validated in April 2026 and a national data governance strategy was validated in 2025, but no official text of either was found, so both are listed as leads.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy
narrative.review_notes: The websites of the Presidency, the National Assembly, the legislation portal, the Senate and the telecom regulator were searched; the 2026 personal data protection law is recorded from the text published by the National Assembly. The national AI strategy and the national data governance strategy have no published official text yet, so they remain listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°1/03 du 10 mars 2026 portant protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 1/03 of 10 March 2026 on the protection of personal data
instruments.current_status: Promulgated at Gitega on 10 March 2026 (signed by President Évariste Ndayishimiye, countersigned by the Minister of Justice). Art. 55: in force on the day of promulgation. Art. 53 gives existing processing one year (State, public bodies, local authorities and bodies with a public-service mission) or six months (others) from entry into force to comply. The text is read from the copy published by the National Assembly on its 'Lois promulguées en 2026' page; the Official Bulletin reference was not found.
instruments.summary: Burundi's first general personal data protection law, issued in French and Kirundi. It sets processing principles and data-subject rights (information, access, rectification, erasure, objection and portability), requires major controllers to register with the personal data protection body and appoint a data protection officer, and sets fines for unlawful processing of sensitive data such as racial or ethnic origin, opinions, health or biometric data (art. 50). Decisions based on automated processing that produce legal or significant effects are allowed only when provided by law with safeguards, with the person's consent, or when strictly necessary for a contract; they must come with an individual explanation, and the person may obtain a new reasoned decision taken by a human that fully replaces the first (arts. 19-20).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems and sets explicit rules on automated decision-making: notice of the automated logic, limited legal bases, an individual explanation and the right to a fresh human decision (arts. 19-20).
